Introduction
Stiff-man syndrome (SMS) is a rare CNS disorder
whose etiology has up to now remained unexplained. Only recently, Solimena et al. [18] provided evidence of an autoimmune pathogencsis
of SMS in two cases, one with type I (autoim-,
mune) diabetes me Uitus (DM), and one with isletcell antibodies (ICA) without DM. In these cases,
the patient serum and CSF harboured specific antibodies to glutamic-acid decarboxylase (GAD).
We therefore report in detail the case of a patient
who developed autoimmune myasthenia gravis
(MG) with thymoma after the remission of SMS...

The associate signs spontaneously cleared within

satisfactory functional condition over the following six years.

were markedly improved by chronic oral diazepare treatment (30 rag/day), which maintained a
satisfactory functional condition over the following six years. At the beginning of October 1979 the
patient suddenly experienced a transitory worsening of muscle stiffness, followed by intermittent
dysphagia, dysarthria and dyspnea. When the patient was admitted again to our Institute, he no
longer had rigidity and presented only facial
weakness and slightly reduced thoracic expansion.

reated by oral pyridostygmine, which markedly
